cls: Sphingosine 1-phosphate (S1P) receptor modulator - disease-modifying therapy for multiple sclerosis
pharm: After phosphorylation to fingolimod-phosphate it binds sphingosine-1-phosphate receptors on lymphocytes, blocking their egress from lymph nodes and reducing peripheral lymphocyte counts, thereby limiting lymphocyte infiltration into the central nervous system.
quick: May be taken with or without food
Can cause fetal harm; effective contraception during and 2 months after stopping
Excreted in animal milk; not recommended while breastfeeding
No dose adjustment in renal impairment
Use caution in severe hepatic impairment; exposure increased
No specific interaction; avoid if hepatic enzymes raised
First-dose 6 h ECG/HR/BP, CBC, LFTs, ophthalmology (macular edema), infection, skin
summary: Fingolimod is a sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor modulator indicated for relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis. The standard dose is 0.5 mg once daily. Because the first dose causes a transient decrease in heart rate and may cause AV conduction block, all patients require first-dose monitoring with ECG and hourly pulse/blood pressure for at least 6 hours after the first dose (extended/overnight monitoring if bradycardia is symptomatic, marked, or if there is QT prolongation or new heart block). Key risks include bradyarrhythmia/AV block, infections (including fatal herpetic and cryptococcal infections and PML), macular edema, decreased pulmonary function, liver injury, and posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome. Severe increase in disability (rebound) has been reported after stopping fingolimod. Obtain a recent CBC, baseline ECG, LFTs, ophthalmologic and dermatologic assessment, and confirm VZV immunity (vaccinate non-immune patients) before starting.
indications: Treatment of relapsing forms of multiple sclerosis, including clinically isolated syndrome, relapsing-remitting disease, and active secondary progressive disease, in adults and pediatric patients aged 10 years and older

dosage.n: Higher doses confer no added benefit and more risk; first-dose cardiac monitoring required

dosage.c: Relapsing MS - pediatric >=10 years and >40 kg
Relapsing MS - pediatric >=10 years and <=40 kg
dosage.n: Lower dose for low body weight

dosage.d: Repeat first-dose 6-hour cardiac monitoring if therapy is interrupted for >14 days (>=1 day in first 2 weeks, >7 days in weeks 3-4)
dosage.n: Bradycardia risk recurs after a treatment gap

admin: Before starting, obtain a recent CBC, baseline ECG, liver transaminases/bilirubin, blood pressure, ophthalmologic evaluation, and skin examination; confirm varicella (VZV) immunity and vaccinate non-immune patients (then delay therapy 1 month)

Administer the FIRST dose where resources to manage symptomatic bradycardia are available; obtain a pre-dose ECG, then monitor with hourly pulse and blood pressure for at least 6 hours and a post-6-hour ECG
Extend cardiac monitoring (continuous ECG overnight) if heart rate at 6 hours is lowest of the day, is <45 bpm (adults), shows new second-degree or higher AV block, or QTc >=500 ms
Repeat first-dose monitoring when therapy is reinitiated after qualifying interruptions
May be taken with or without food, at the same time each day
Counsel women of reproductive potential on contraception during and for 2 months after stopping
moa: Fingolimod is metabolized by sphingosine kinase to its active metabolite, fingolimod-phosphate, a modulator of sphingosine-1-phosphate (S1P) receptors. By binding with high affinity to S1P receptors 1, 3, 4 and 5 on lymphocytes, it blocks the capacity of lymphocytes to egress from lymph nodes, causing a reversible redistribution (sequestration) of lymphocytes into lymphoid tissue and a reduction in peripheral blood lymphocyte counts. This reduces the migration of pathogenic lymphocytes into the central nervous system, decreasing central inflammation. S1P receptors are also expressed on cardiac and other cells, accounting for the transient negative chronotropic effect on first dosing.

absolute: Myocardial infarction, unstable angina, stroke/TIA, or decompensated heart failure (requiring hospitalization) or Class III/IV heart failure in the previous 6 months
Mobitz type II second-degree or third-degree AV block or sick sinus syndrome, unless the patient has a functioning pacemaker
Treatment with Class Ia or Class III antiarrhythmic drugs
Known hypersensitivity to fingolimod or any component
relative: Patients on heart-rate-lowering drugs (beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers)
History of recurrent syncope, bradycardia, or significant prolonged QT
Active or chronic infections, immunosuppression, or no documented VZV immunity
Diabetes mellitus or history of uveitis (macular edema risk)
monitor: Heart rate, blood pressure and ECG (first dose and after interruptions)
Ophthalmologic examination 3-4 months after start and as needed (macular edema)
Signs of infection (including herpetic, cryptococcal, PML)
Blood pressure during chronic therapy; skin examination for malignancy

preg: Based on animal data, fingolimod can cause fetal harm, including embryolethality and teratogenicity (visceral and skeletal malformations), when given during pregnancy. Women of reproductive potential should use effective contraception during treatment and for 2 months after stopping, because the drug takes about 2 months to be eliminated. Avoid use in pregnancy; a pregnancy exposure registry exists.
lact: Fingolimod is excreted in the milk of treated animals. There are no data on its presence in human milk or effects on the breastfed infant. Because of the potential for serious adverse reactions in the infant, breastfeeding is not recommended during fingolimod therapy.
renal: The pharmacokinetics of fingolimod are not meaningfully altered by renal impairment, and no dose adjustment is required in patients with renal impairment.
hepatic: Fingolimod can cause elevations of liver transaminases; obtain transaminase and bilirubin levels before starting and monitor during treatment. Exposure to the active metabolite is increased in severe hepatic impairment, so use caution in these patients. Discontinue if significant liver injury occurs.

major: Class Ia and Class III antiarrhythmics (e.g., quinidine, amiodarone, sotalol) - contraindicated; risk of torsades and additive bradyarrhythmia
Live attenuated vaccines - avoid during and for 2 months after therapy (risk of infection; reduced vaccine efficacy)
Other immunosuppressants/immune-modulating therapies - additive immunosuppression and infection risk
moderate: Beta-blockers and non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blockers - additive heart-rate lowering; assess before starting
Ketoconazole and other strong CYP4F2/CYP3A inhibitors - increase fingolimod exposure
Strong CYP3A4 inducers (e.g., carbamazepine, rifampin) - decrease fingolimod exposure
minor: QT-prolonging drugs - use with caution given transient first-dose effects
interactions.food: Food has no clinically significant effect on absorption; may be taken with or without food.
interactions.alcohol: No specific interaction described; limit alcohol if liver enzymes are elevated.
interactions.diagnostics: Reduces peripheral lymphocyte counts (expected, dose-related); may elevate liver transaminases. Lymphocyte counts do not reflect total body immune status.

serious: Bradyarrhythmia and AV conduction block (especially after first dose)
Serious infections (herpetic, cryptococcal meningitis, opportunistic) and progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (PML)
Cutaneous and other malignancies (basal cell carcinoma, melanoma, lymphoma)
rare: Severe increase in disability (rebound) after discontinuation
emergency: Symptomatic or severe bradycardia/heart block after first dose
Signs of PML or cryptococcal meningitis (new neurologic deficits, headache, confusion)
Posterior reversible encephalopathy syndrome (severe headache, seizures, visual disturbance)
Severe disability rebound after stopping the drug

monitoring: First-dose cardiac monitoring: pre-dose ECG, hourly pulse and blood pressure for 6 hours, post-6-hour ECG (extend/overnight if criteria met); repeat after qualifying interruptions
Complete blood count (lymphocytes) at baseline and periodically
Liver transaminases and bilirubin at baseline and during treatment
Ophthalmologic examination at 3-4 months and with any visual symptoms (macular edema)
Skin examination for melanoma and basal cell carcinoma; vigilance for infection signs
counsel: Your first dose will be given where you can be watched for at least 6 hours because the drug can slow your heart rate
Take one tablet at the same time each day, with or without food; do not stop without telling your doctor (your MS can flare badly if you stop suddenly)
Report any new infection, fever, persistent cough, breathlessness, or yellowing of the skin/eyes promptly
Have your eyes checked as advised - report blurred vision, blind spots, or sensitivity to light (macular edema)
Tell your doctor about any chest symptoms, fainting, or irregular heartbeat
Use reliable contraception during treatment and for 2 months after stopping; tell your doctor if you become pregnant or plan to
Avoid live vaccines during and for 2 months after treatment; protect your skin from the sun and report new skin lesions
pk: Lymphocyte counts fall within 4-6 hours of first dose; first-dose heart-rate decrease within 6 hours
Plasma Tmax 12-16 hours; steady state in 1-2 months
Effects (lymphopenia, drug presence) persist up to ~2 months after stopping
Store at 25 C (excursions 15-30 C permitted); protect from moisture
pearls: First-dose effect: transient bradycardia and possible AV block - all patients need ECG plus 6-hour pulse/BP monitoring after the first dose (and after qualifying interruptions)
Macular edema risk - obtain baseline and 3-4 month ophthalmologic exams, sooner in diabetes or prior uveitis
Infection risk includes fatal herpetic and cryptococcal infections and PML; confirm VZV immunity and vaccinate non-immune patients before starting
Rebound: severe worsening of MS (disability rebound) can occur after stopping - do not discontinue abruptly without a plan
Long half-life (~6-9 days) - lymphopenia and pregnancy/vaccine precautions persist ~2 months after the last dose
Avoid live vaccines during and for 2 months after therapy
missed: If you miss a dose, take the next dose at your usual time. However, if treatment is interrupted for more than 1 day during the first 2 weeks, more than 7 days in weeks 3-4, or more than 14 days after the first month, contact your doctor before resuming - you will need the first-dose 6-hour heart monitoring again.
overdose: Single doses up to 40 times the recommended dose have been tolerated, but overdose may cause symptomatic bradycardia and AV block. Monitor with continuous ECG and blood pressure overnight; treat symptomatic bradycardia with atropine or isoprenaline as needed. Fingolimod is not removed by dialysis or plasma exchange. Provide supportive care.
